qa.q: Which places in your city are crowded?
qa.a: I suppose it depends which city you mean, because, um, in Moscow there are usually throngs of people, but obviously not at the moment because it's the quarantine and we have self-isolation. But usually there are lots of us. Um, and in my hometown in Dundee, there isn't usually a ton of people in open spaces like parks or at the beach, even when it's sunny. Uh, although I suppose in some clubs it can be a real rammy.

qa.q: Why are those places so crowded?
qa.a: Hmm, in the case of Moscow, I imagine it's because it's a major world capital with literally millions of people. I can't remember how many people that live here. It's something like 15 million, so that's a lot. It doesn't matter how widespread your city is, it's still going to be quite crowded. Uh, by contrast, Dundee is a university town. We've got two universities and they have a lot of students. I imagine that's why the bars and clubs are always full of people. Um, but probably why the libraries aren't as frequented as as they are there. At the same time, it's got a big working-class population, so the local neighborhood pubs must be quite as packed. Um, well, if people are having a drink after a long day, I suppose.

qa.q: How do you feel in these crowded places?
qa.a: Uh, usually I don't mind them. Um, as long as I can make my way through them. Um, but it's always a pain when there's a big crowd and you need the bathroom or you have to wait for a drink or something like that, and you have to wait for ages.

qa.q: Have you ever felt comfortable in a very crowded place?
qa.a: Um, like I say, it's not normally a problem for me, but if I had to choose, I wouldn't be in a place that's borderline overcrowded. Uh, first of all, I like having my personal space respected and secondly, there's always an element of danger in these things.

qa.q: If I were to ask you to describe a crowded place that you've been to, what would you say?
qa.a: Oh, I'd probably, there's, there's a club, um, in my hometown. I'm not sure if it's still open now, but it's almost completely underground, and because of that, the space is quite limited. So, it gets filled up with people really quickly. Um, and that would be the, the image that comes to mind. So everyone has their backs against the wall, or they're sort of crushed in this crowd while they're waiting to dance or at the bar, but you can't really dance and you can't really get a drink. I've no idea why it's so popular.

qa.q: Could you imagine that the most crowded place would be like our home, our flat, our house? So there would be no stadiums, no concerts, nothing.
qa.a: Yeah, well, I suppose our houses are the closest thing we get to being in a crowded space now. Although, even for me now, I only live with like one other person, so it's not so much of a crowd. But no, I definitely couldn't have imagined that that would be the case now.
